heroHeadline: Kyiv Drone Barrage Kills 7 Including Teen as Ukraine's Steel Industry Grinds to a Halt
heroSubtitle: Russian drones struck Kyiv for hours from before dawn on September 25, killing 7 (including a 14-year-old boy) and injuring 59 across the Pecherskyi, Shevchenkivskyi and Solomianskyi districts, part of a nationwide barrage of 295 attack drones that also killed 2 and injured 2 in an overnight strike on Odesa. Ukraine's Defense Forces retaliated the same night with long-range drone strikes roughly 1,500 km inside Russia, hitting the Perm and Novoshakhtinsk oil refineries, the Iskra defense plant in Ulyanovsk, two Rostov radar stations, and synthetic rubber plants in Tula and Voronezh. Separately, ArcelorMittal announced on September 26 it can no longer safely operate its Kryvyi Rih plant — Ukraine's largest steelmaker — after four Russian missile strikes in five weeks killed 5 workers and injured 17, booking a roughly $1 billion impairment charge and leaving all three of Ukraine's main steel plants, once ~90% of national output, offline.
